title: Rebuilding this site, properly this time
summary: From an under-construction placeholder to a fully tested, CI-gated static site with its own Azure Function-backed contact form.
content:
## Why rebuild?

My old site had drifted into "under construction" limbo for longer than I'd like to admit. Rather than patch it, I decided to start from scratch, and use the process as a proper vehicle to level up a few things I'd been meaning to get serious about: test automation on real front-end work, and actually finishing a personal project end to end rather than leaving it half-built.

## The stack

No frameworks, no build step. Just plain HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, served as static files. Each page (Home, Blog, Profile, Projects, Contact) fetches its own content from small JSON files, so adding a new project or blog post is a data change, not a code change.

## Testing it properly

Since I work in test automation professionally, it felt wrong to ship a personal site with zero coverage. I brought in [PRAT](https://github.com/gwuxdesign/PRAT.Template), my own Playwright and Reqnroll-based framework, and wrote real BDD-style feature files for navigation, the blog, projects, the profile page, and the contact form's validation. Every page now has a page object and matching step definitions behind it.

That coverage runs automatically too: a GitHub Actions workflow triggers on every pull request, spins up the site locally, and runs the full suite before anything's allowed to merge.

## The contact form (the hard part)

This ended up being the most involved piece by far. Rather than reach for a third-party form service, I built a proper backend for it: an Azure Function (isolated worker, .NET) that verifies a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge server-side, then sends the message through SendGrid, with an auto-reply confirmation going back to whoever submitted it, original message included.

Along the way I picked up a genuinely useful lesson the hard way: a secret key I'd committed locally got flagged by GitGuardian within hours of pushing. Rotating the key and properly gitignoring the settings file afterwards was a good, if slightly stressful, reminder that "local only" config needs to actually be *told* to stay local.

## What's next

The foundations are solid now: real content, real test coverage, a real CI gate, and a genuinely working contact form, CAPTCHA, email delivery, and all. From here it's about building out the content itself: more posts, more projects, and finally tracking down the old Profile page design I thought I'd lost for good.
